  REMOVE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-13 | Drop 'the settings command is not a toolbar item': current guidance puts Settings among the last items of the toolbar's More menu, or on the toolbar itself when it must be easy to find.
## CMD-3
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-04 | On Windows the app's facts (version, copyright, privacy policy) sit in an About section at the bottom of the Settings page, and Settings is reached from the navigation pane or toolbar, not Tools > Options; Exit is unaffected.
## CMD-8
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-24 | About is no longer the last item of the Help menu: it is a section at the bottom of the Settings page showing the app's name, icon and version, expanding to more.
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-32 | About is no longer the last item of the Help menu: it is a section at the bottom of the Settings page showing the app's name, icon and version, expanding to more.
## CTL-10
  CHANGE ui-controls-tab-view-03 | Beyond a few static pages, prefer a navigation pane (a vertical list at the leading side) to a tab row; Fluent gives no number, so seven stays the ceiling for a tab row, not the target.
  CHANGE ui-controls-selector-bar-01 | A short tab-like row of view selectors may switch between a few views or filters of the same data (All, Unread, Flagged); a select or split button stays for many views.
  CHANGE ui-controls-selector-bar-02 | A short tab-like row of view selectors may switch between a few views or filters of the same data (All, Unread, Flagged); a select or split button stays for many views.
## CTL-11
  CHANGE ui-controls-tree-view-04 | Windows: a tree only when seeing the hierarchy matters; drilling into a hierarchy level by level uses a plain list, even past two levels (drop 'a tree for any hierarchy deeper than two levels').
## CTL-15
  CHANGE basics-titlebar-design-18 | Windows: app-wide search is a box centred in the title bar; a search of one view stays at that view's top trailing corner.
  CHANGE ui-controls-listview-filtering-04 | A filter over a list keeps items containing the typed text anywhere, not only at word starts (from the page's worked example; owner to weigh against 'search matches the starts of words').
## CTL-16
  CHANGE ui-controls-expander-03 | Windows form: several expandable sections may stack in one view (as in Windows 11 Settings), each opened independently; 'at most one per view' applies only to an advanced-options disclosure.
## CTL-2
  CHANGE ui-controls-checkbox-12 | Windows: any on/off setting that takes effect at once is a switch (not only large-scope ones); a check box is for a choice committed later with its form or dialog, or for multiple selection.
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-06 | On a settings page, whose changes apply at once, a binary setting is a switch rather than a checkbox.
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-07 | Radio buttons for two to five options, as on macOS; six or more go in a select (Windows 7 allowed up to seven).
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-34 | On a settings page, whose changes apply at once, a binary setting is a switch rather than a checkbox.
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-35 | Radio buttons for two to five options, as on macOS; six or more go in a select (Windows 7 allowed up to seven).
  CHANGE ui-controls-combo-box-03 | Radio buttons for two to four options; five or more may go in a select (Fluent: fewer than five), close to the macOS form; replaces 'two to seven, eight or more in a select'.
  CHANGE ui-controls-combo-box-09 | Radio buttons for two to four fixed options (same change as fluent-ui-controls-combo-box-03).
  REMOVE ui-controls-radio-button-04 | Drop 'on a page of a guided flow, radio buttons even where a checkbox would do': Fluent says a single binary choice is one checkbox or switch, never two radio buttons (I agree / I don't agree).
  CHANGE ui-controls-radio-button-07 | Radio buttons for two to eight options; more than eight go in a select or list (was: eight or more).
  CHANGE ui-controls-forms-20 | Windows form: radio buttons or checkboxes for up to four options; five or more go in a list or select (Windows 7 allowed radio buttons up to seven).
## CTL-26
  CHANGE ui-controls-hyperlinks-03 | A picture may be a link when it has an accessible name saying where it goes; Windows 7's 'never a picture alone' is looser now.
  REMOVE ui-controls-hyperlinks-04 | Drop 'runs a light, harmless command' and 'a command inside running text, or one needing five or more words, is a link': links now only navigate, actions are buttons (also drops WRD-18's 'adds now' case).
  CHANGE ui-controls-hyperlinks-07 | Every link, not only a web link, has a tooltip saying where it leads; for a website the tooltip names its top-level domain.
## CTL-5
  REMOVE ui-controls-checkbox-15 | Drop the Windows 7 cycle back to the original mix: people never set the mixed state directly, so a click on a mixed check box turns all on and the next turns all off.
## CTL-8
  CHANGE ui-controls-forms-07 | Windows form: the submit button may stay disabled until every required field is filled (bears on Q-30); with that, the required fields are marked so the reason is visible.
## CTL-9
  CHANGE ui-controls-number-box-07 | Stepping stops at the limits and the step button that would pass the minimum or maximum is disabled; drop 'stepping past an end wraps'.
  CHANGE ui-controls-number-box-08 | The step buttons sit beside the number field (or appear only while it has focus), not inside the box.
## FDB-2
  CHANGE ui-controls-progress-controls-09 | Allow an indeterminate ring while the app waits on a step the reader is completing elsewhere (signing in through a browser); 'never the reader's work' keeps meaning work done in the window itself.
## HLP-6
  CHANGE in-app-help-external-help-05 | Windows: link to the topic for the place wherever one exists; where none does, a link to a help home organised by categories is acceptable (loosens 'never a link to the help home').
## KEY-2
  CHANGE ui-controls-tab-view-17 | Ctrl+W closes the selected tab or document window, now from Microsoft's own guidance (TabView), not only common practice.
## KEY-5
  CHANGE ui-controls-tab-view-16 | In an app with document tabs Ctrl+T (new tab), Ctrl+W, Ctrl+Shift+T and Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+9 (go to tab) are taken by tab commands, so they are no longer free for other commands.
## KEY-6
  CHANGE ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-28 | Windows: a dialog need not have a default button; give one only when one answer is clearly the likely and safe one, and without one Enter presses only a focused button.
## LAY-5
  CHANGE ui-controls-buttons-23 | Windows: on a page inside the window (not a dialog) a single button aligns at the leading edge with the page's content; dialogs keep their buttons at the trailing corner.
## LAY-6
  CHANGE ui-controls-forms-10 | Windows form: a field's label sits above it, aligned with its leading edge; the label beside the field on its baseline is no longer the Windows default.
## MSG-4
  CHANGE ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-05 | Windows: a simple message, error or question may have no title, its first line of content then saying what happened or asking the question; the message-box caption naming the command no longer applies.
## MSG-6
  CHANGE ui-controls-forms-08 | Windows form: problems found when a form is submitted are marked at each field in error (with words, not colour alone) and the form stays open for resubmission, instead of a dialog.
## Q-1
  ANSWERS ui-controls-menus-and-context-menus-09 | Current guidance treats the menu bar as optional: use one when commands need several top-level menus, otherwise a menu from a button (and a command bar); it does not require a menu bar on every main window.
  ANSWERS basics-commanding-basics-06 | Fluent makes the command bar the default and a menu bar the choice for an app too complex for a command bar, so a simple Kvit app may do without a menu bar on Windows.
  ANSWERS basics-app-silhouette-03 | Windows 11 keeps a menu bar (with a command bar beside it) for editing apps such as Notepad; navigation apps use a sidebar or top navigation instead.
## Q-15
  ANSWERS style-writing-style-10 | Microsoft now recommends we for the app's own perspective (We couldn't save your file to that location), not only sparingly for the maker.
## Q-2
  ANSWERS ui-controls-navigationview-04 | Current Windows guidance puts Settings in the navigation pane (its last item) as a page of the app, not as Tools > Options in a modal window.
  ANSWERS app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-01 | Settings is a dedicated page in the app's window, not a modal Options dialog, and it applies changes at once.
  ANSWERS ui-controls-forms-01 | Current Windows guidance: settings pages apply each change immediately (no OK/Cancel), against WIN-16/WIN-23's Windows 7 form of a modal Options window committed on OK.
## Q-26
  ANSWERS ui-controls-number-box-09 | Current Windows places the stepper buttons beside the field (inline) or in a small popup shown only while the field is focused; neither is inside the box as in Windows 7.
## Q-28
  ANSWERS ui-controls-text-box-10 | Current Windows guidance allows a checkbox to reveal its dependent text fields (to reduce clutter) as well as to enable them; its list-box page still says a list must not show or hide other controls.
## Q-29
  ANSWERS app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-33 | A settings page is a single column that scrolls when it does not fit; the no-scroll rule applies to dialogs and flow pages, not to the settings page.
## Q-3
  ANSWERS style-writing-style-19 | Windows: one capitalisation for every string, sentence case (first word and proper nouns), labels and titles alike.
## Q-32
  ANSWERS ui-controls-progress-controls-19 | Current Fluent still allows a brief wait (busy) pointer over the app or the area that should not be used until it disappears, so Windows keeps the busy pointer for short waits.
## Q-34
  ANSWERS in-app-help-in-app-help-03 | Current Microsoft guidance keeps short instructions and tips in the app and hosts complex instructions and tutorials outside it (online).
## Q-35
  ANSWERS ui-controls-color-picker-03 | Microsoft scales the colour picker to the task: a simple one (hue ring and slider, no value fields) for casual choices, a full one with value fields for precise work, rather than always the system's dialog.
## Q-37
  ANSWERS app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-22 | Microsoft's theme setting is a select with Light, Dark and Use system setting, optionally with a link to the system's colour settings.
  ANSWERS signature-experiences-color-01 | Current Windows guidance: an app follows the system light/dark theme by default and may offer its own theme setting, which supports a Kvit appearance setting defaulting to the desktop's.
## Q-5
  ANSWERS ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-30 | Current guidance still names the OK/Cancel pattern but asks for specific response labels and never mentions Yes/No; it supports specific verbs over OK and Yes/No, and its own examples use Close or Got it, not OK, for a dismiss-only message.
  ANSWERS ui-controls-buttons-11 | The current Buttons page still lists OK and Yes/No in the commit order beside specific responses ([Do it], [Don't do it]); OK and Yes/No are not dropped on Windows, though the dialogs page prefers specific labels.
## Q-7
  ANSWERS ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-16 | Current Windows guidance makes the default button optional (none unless set), unlike Windows 7's every-dialog-has-one.
## Q-9
  ANSWERS ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-03 | Current Windows dialogs have no caption naming the command or program: the title is the main instruction (MSG-4 and WIN-6 Windows forms should drop the Windows 7 caption).
## WIN-1
  CHANGE ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-24 | Windows: left to right, the main action, an optional second action (a neutral alternative, not No), then the safe button (Cancel, Close or a specific negative) at the right end.
## WIN-10
  CHANGE ui-controls-color-picker-06 | Windows: a popover with explicit commit and Cancel buttons discards its changes on a click outside; one without them keeps what was entered.
## WIN-11
  CHANGE ui-controls-navigationview-26 | Windows: the title bar may hold the back button, the sidebar toggle, an app-wide search box and the account picture (Kvit draws it), as long as empty parts still drag the window; it no longer has to hold no app controls.
  CHANGE ui-controls-tab-view-15 | On Windows document tabs may sit in the title bar, provided a free part of it is always left for dragging the window; otherwise the frame holds no app controls.
  CHANGE ui-controls-title-bar-03 | Windows form: the title bar may hold a few app controls (Back, the sidebar toggle, a search box, tabs), provided an empty drag area remains beside the caption buttons; the general rule's 'holds no app controls' no longer holds on Windows 11.
## WIN-16
  CHANGE ui-controls-navigationview-07 | In a window with a navigation sidebar, Settings (named Settings, not Options) is the sidebar's last item, below footer items such as Help, and opens a settings page in the window; Tools > Options in a modal OK/Cancel window remains only for menu-bar apps without a sidebar.
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-12 | The command is Settings (not Options), opening the Settings page; with a navigation pane it is the pane's last item pinned to the bottom; changes apply at once.
  REMOVE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-41 | Drop 'opens a modal window titled Options with OK and Cancel, its changes taken on OK': current guidance forbids a confirmation button on settings.
## WIN-2
  CHANGE ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-07 | Windows: a dialog always has body text; with a title it adds detail, without one it carries the message itself.
  CHANGE ui-controls-buttons-12 | Windows: a decision shows one or two buttons; further actions become checkboxes or radio buttons committed by one button; a third button only sparingly.
## WIN-23
  CHANGE app-settings-guidelines-for-app-settings-10 | App settings apply each change at once and have no OK, Cancel or Apply, as on macOS; OK, Cancel and Apply stay only for a properties dialog of one object.
## WIN-6
  CHANGE ui-controls-dialogs-and-flyouts-dialogs-04 | Windows: a dialog's title is its main instruction, a short statement of what to do or decide; it no longer names the command, feature or program it came from.
## WRD-14
  CHANGE style-writing-style-02 | Windows form: a problem message has the app take responsibility in the active voice (We couldn't save your file) rather than avoiding blame with the passive.
## WRD-17
  CHANGE style-writing-style-06 | Windows form: current Microsoft text uses select for buttons and commands too (Select filters, select save); allow select as the input-neutral verb instead of requiring click.
## WRD-19
  REMOVE ui-controls-labels-04 | Drop 'a label ends with a colon (Name:)' from the Windows form, and the same colon from WRD-20's group labels and CTL-5's dependent-control labels; settles Q-22.
  CHANGE ui-controls-text-box-05 | Looser than the rule: Fluent lets a placeholder stand in for the visible label wherever the field's purpose is otherwise clear, not only in search and cramped toolbar fields; the label stays required where it is not (owner to decide whether to loosen).
  CHANGE ui-controls-text-box-06 | The prompt stays while the field is focused and empty, disappears once a value is entered and returns when the field is emptied (as on macOS); drop 'disappears when the field takes focus'.
  CHANGE ui-controls-slider-28 | Drop the colon: a control's label, beside or above it, ends without punctuation, which current Fluent states as the convention for all control labels (settles Q-22 for Windows).
  CHANGE ui-controls-number-box-03 | Looser than the rule: Fluent lets a placeholder stand in for the visible label wherever the field's purpose is otherwise clear, not only in search and cramped toolbar fields (owner to decide whether to loosen).
  CHANGE ui-controls-number-box-04 | The prompt shows whenever the field is empty and goes once a value is entered, focused or not (as on macOS); drop 'disappears when the field takes focus'.
  CHANGE ui-controls-password-box-02 | Fluent lets a placeholder alone name a field whose purpose is clear from context, but notes only a label stays visible once a value is entered; keep the visible label as the default and allow placeholder-only where context makes the field obvious (such as a sign-in pair).
  CHANGE ui-controls-password-box-03 | Windows form: the prompt stays while the field is focused and empty and disappears at the first character typed, returning when the field is emptied (not on focus, as Windows 7 had it).
## WRD-2
  CHANGE ui-controls-command-bar-11 | Windows: a toolbar button's label is preferably one word (longer labels wrap); Windows 7's up to four words is the outer limit, not the norm.
  CHANGE style-writing-style-25 | Windows form: a button is at most a couple of short words; drop the four-word allowance for labelled toolbar buttons.
## WRD-21
  CHANGE ui-controls-buttons-03 | Windows: a guided flow's Back is a button labelled Back beside Next among the bottom buttons, not an unlabelled arrow at the top leading corner.
## WRD-25
  CHANGE ui-controls-progress-controls-07 | Looser: Fluent lists Loading..., Retrieving and Working... as ordinary text beside a progress bar; the Windows form could accept such a word where the object is obvious from context (owner to decide; the stricter rule is not contradicted outright).
## WRD-6
  CHANGE signature-experiences-typography-04 | Windows form: sentence case for all text, including window and dialog titles and a guided flow's name; title case is no longer used anywhere.
